title: Nearest points in finite-dimensional subspaces of discretely valued ultrametric spaces
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime and let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite with its extended nonarchimedean norm [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $V$ be an $E$-vector space with a norm satisfying $\|av\|=|a|\|v\|$, $\|v+w\|\leq\max(\|v\|,\|w\|)$, and definiteness. If $W\subseteq V$ is a finite-dimensional $E$-linear subspace and $x\in V$, then there is $w_0\in W$ such that
$$\|x-w_0\|=\inf_{w\in W}\|x-w\|.$$ 
If $x\notin W$, this infimum is strictly positive. No completeness of $V$ is required.

proof.text: Give $W$ its restricted norm and write $r=\|x\|$. The ultrametric inequality implies the usual triangle inequality. By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-proper], closed balls in $E$ are compact, so each point has a compact neighbourhood (its closed ball of radius $1$). Thus $E$ is locally compact. Its absolute value is nontrivial since $|\ell|=\ell^{-1}<1$. These observations supply the scalar hypotheses of the finite-dimensional properness theorem.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-finite-dimensional-normed-proper] with $K=E$ and $Y=W$, which is finite-dimensional by hypothesis and has a definite homogeneous restricted norm. The set $C=\{w\in W:\|w\|\leq r\}$ is consequently compact in $W$. It is nonempty because $0\in W$ and $r\geq0$. This applies also when $r=0$ or $W=0$.

proof.text: Define $f:W\to\mathbf R$ by $f(w)=\|x-w\|$. For $u,v\in W$, the ordinary triangle inequality gives $f(u)\leq f(v)+\|u-v\|$ and $f(v)\leq f(u)+\|u-v\|$. Hence $|f(u)-f(v)|\leq\|u-v\|$, proving continuity of $f$ on $W$ and therefore on $C$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-compact-real-function-minimum] to the nonempty compact subset $C$ of the normed space $W$ and the continuous real function $f$. Obtain $w_0\in C$ with $f(w_0)\leq f(w)$ for all $w\in C$. In particular, since $0\in C$, $f(w_0)\leq f(0)=r$.

proof.text: If $w\in W\setminus C$, then $\|w\|>r$. Ultrametricity gives $f(w)\leq\max(r,\|w\|)=\|w\|$ and $\|w\|\leq\max(r,f(w))$, using $w=x-(x-w)$. The latter inequality and $\|w\|>r$ force $\|w\|\leq f(w)$. Therefore $f(w)=\|w\|>r\geq f(w_0)$. Together with the minimum inequality on $C$, this proves that $w_0$ minimizes $f$ over all of $W$.

proof.text: The set $\{\|x-w\|:w\in W\}$ is nonempty and bounded below by $0$. Its member $f(w_0)$ is a lower bound by the previous step, so it equals the infimum. If $x\notin W$, then $x-w_0\ne0$ because $w_0\in W$. Definiteness gives $f(w_0)>0$. Only the restricted norm on $W$ and its compact ball were used; the ambient space $V$ was never assumed complete.

The statement is unchanged, so the citer still gets the nearest point it needs. The proof checks out step by step. Step 1: E is proper, hence locally compact, and |l|=1/l<1 makes it nontrivially normed. Step 2: the ball C of radius r=||x|| in W is compact by FiniteDimensional.proper with K=E, Y=W; no completeness or properness of V is used. Step 3: w -> ||x-w|| is 1-Lipschitz, so continuous. Step 4: it attains a minimum w0 on C, and f(w0)<=f(0)=r. Step 5: for ||w||>r, the two ultrametric inequalities give f(w)=||w||>r, so w0 is a global minimum; no value-group discreteness is needed. Step 6: the infimum is attained and is positive by definiteness when x is not in W. Small cases checked: the Gauss norm on Q_l(t) with W=Q_l and x=t; W=0; x in W; a case with several nearest points; incomplete V. Both leaves are exact or one-line Mathlib matches with lines given and all three search kinds recorded. The proper leaf shares its declaration with lem-weil-l-adic-extension-proper, but that node is only the special case K=Q_l, Y=E and cannot give compactness of balls in an arbitrary normed E-space W, so the new node is not a duplicate. No DAG node carries exists_isMinOn. No new node restates a clause of the item, there is no cycle, proof_deps equals the union of the step uses, no SGA is cited, and this is not a re-split under a repair note.
